title: Bounded flat coefficient complex
statement: For a qcqs scheme X, E in the bounded-below derived category of etale integer-module sheaves and P a complex of flat integer modules zero outside a finite interval [b,N], the canonical counit-mate map RΓ(E) tensor^L Q(P) to RΓ(E tensor^L constant(Q(P))) is an isomorphism. Definitions are those of [def-kun-constant-projection-morphism], [def-kun-derived-tensor] and [def-sbc-standard-tstructure-derived-category].

proof.text: On K-flat representatives use the cone matrix (d,u;0,-d): tensor distributes over the two summands, naturality supplies the off-diagonal u-square, and the shifted signs agree. The derived constant tensor comparison and counit therefore give compatible morphisms of triangles in either variable. Under the normalized constant unit constraint the adjunction triangle identity makes the unit comparison identity. These are also the existing generic Adjunction.ProjectionMapShift and ProjectionMapUnit calculations; no change to SheafOfModules is required.

proof.text: For a flat module M and a sheaf F in degree zero, use Lazard to write M as a directed colimit of finite free modules. Constant sheaves and ordinary tensor preserve this colimit. Qcqs cohomology commutes with it on the target. On the source, flatness gives H^q(RΓ(F) tensor^L M) = H^q(RΓ(F)) tensor M by preserving the kernel-image sequences of a complex; ordinary module tensor preserves the colimit. The finite free comparison is a finite sum of the unit comparison. Naturality identifies the two systems, so the colimit comparison is invertible. Negative degrees vanish. This uses no general filtered-colimit theorem for derived tensor.

proof.text: Keep K=M[0] flat and now let E be arbitrary bounded below. Flatness means that tensor preserves the kernel-image short exact sequences of a complex, whence $H^i(C\otimes M)=H^i(C)\otimes M$; the same holds for $\underline M$ on sheaves, since constant sheaves preserve flat objects. Fix n and put $E_n=\tau_{\le n}E$. By [lem-weil-pbc-derived-functor-truncation-iso], $RE_n\to RE$ induces an isomorphism on $H^n$. Exact flat tensor gives the same for the source comparisons, and $E_n\otimes\underline M\to E\otimes\underline M$ has isomorphic cohomology through n and a monomorphism in degree n+1; the same cited truncation lemma gives the target isomorphism in degree n. The object E_n has cohomology in only finitely many degrees. Starting with its lowest nonzero cohomology sheaf, successively use the canonical triangles $\tau_{\le j-1}E_n\to\tau_{\le j}E_n\to H^j(E_n)[-j]\to$ from [lem-weil-pbc-truncation-triangle]. The flat-module case handles each sheaf, shifts are handled by step 1, and the long exact cohomology sequences of the morphisms of triangles propagate the isomorphism by the five lemma. This proves the comparison for E_n and hence in degree n for E. Since n was arbitrary, it proves the flat-group case for every E.

source.place: Tag 0F0E (lemma-pull-out-constant), repeating the truncation argument for E, with the degree bound written out

proof.text: For fixed E, let P be a bounded complex of flat abelian groups. Induct on the number of its potentially nonzero terms. The zero complex is immediate; a single term is a shift of the flat-group case. For a complex supported in [b,N], the degreewise split short exact sequence $0\to\sigma_{\ge b+1}P\to P\to P^b[-b]\to0$ gives the stupid truncation triangle. Step 1 turns the comparison into a morphism of triangles. The first and third comparisons are isomorphisms by induction and the flat-group case; exactness of the cohomology sequences gives the middle isomorphism. This establishes all bounded flat coefficient complexes.
